newsitem.title: USA: Lott sees Senate budget amendment OK this week.
newsitem.headline: Lott sees Senate budget amendment OK this week.

text.p: Senate Majority Leader Trent Lott said the balanced budget agreement has "a lot of momentum" and he expects the Senate to approve it this week.
"I think this thing has a lot of momentum," Lott told reporters after a speech to the National Association of Realtors.
But he noted that the budget agreement is the hurdle that must be cleared "to get to the real legislation" -- the more detailed spending and tax bill.
At the realtors convention, he said that he had several goals in the tax part of the budget deal but cutting capital gains taxes, to 19.8 percent or lower, was his priority.
He said if President Clinton threatens to veto the tax bill, "I'm prepared to call his bluff."
The bipartisan budget plan aims to eliminate the deficit in five years. It cuts spending by $304 billion over the five years below what would have occurred without changes in policy.
It provides for a net $85 billion tax cut by 2002 and gives Clinton $33 billion for domestic goals.
